'''Soto padang''' is a kind of clear, non [[coconut milk]]ed [[Soto (food)|soto]], which usually contains [[beef]], [[onion]], [[potato]]es, and [[rice vermicelli|white vermicelli noodles]] as its main ingredients.<ref name="Margi">{{cite web
| title = A tasty bite of Indonesia
| url = http://www.nationmultimedia.com/travel/A-tasty-bite-of-Indonesia-30246416.html
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141110155028/http://www.nationmultimedia.com/travel/A-tasty-bite-of-Indonesia-30246416.html
| url-status = dead
| archive-date = November 10, 2014
| first = Raditya | last = Margi
| publisher = [[The Nation]]
| date = October 29, 2014
| access-date = October 12, 2017
| others = @ Copyright 2017 by The Nation
}}</ref> This soto is a culinary specialty originating from [[West Sumatra]], [[Indonesia]].<ref name="Margi"/><ref>{{cite web
| title = The Harmony Restaurant celebrates Indonesian cuisine with 'Selera Nusantara' event
| url = http://www.thejakartapost.com/life/2017/05/07/the-harmony-restaurant-celebrates-indonesian-cuisine-with-selera-nusantara-event.html
| publisher = [[The Jakarta Post]]
| date = May 7, 2017
| access-date = October 12, 2017
| others = © 2017 PT. Niskala Media Tenggara
}}</ref><ref name="Von Holzen"/> 

The meat used for the soto can be boiled and cut,<ref name="Von Holzen"/> or it can be fried until crunchy.<ref name="Margi"/> The potatoes are boiled, then seasoned and made into small patties and then fried.<ref name="Von Holzen"/> Individual bowls are prepared with rice vermicelli, meat and potatoes put inside, and boiled egg can be added before the broth is poured in.<ref name="Von Holzen"/> Sliced celery, scallions, and fried shallot are usually added as garnishes.<ref name="Von Holzen"/>

In [[Padang|Padang City]], this soto is often served for breakfast, and sometimes accompanied by the ''[[teh talua]]'' (creamed egg tea).<ref name="Von Holzen">{{cite book
